title: Hex standoff with an M4 stud and an M4 tapped hole

description.en: A hexagonal standoff (male-female) for M4: a hex 8 mm across flats and 20 mm long standing on the XY plane, its axis the Z axis and two of its corners on the X axis. On top, an M4 stud 8 mm long (a 4 mm cylinder) with an external M4 thread over 6.5 mm from its free end; in the bottom, a tapped hole: a 3.3 mm tap drill 10 mm deep with an internal M4 thread over 8 mm from the bottom face. Threads may be cosmetic. Drive it by the variables across_flats, length, stud_len and tap_depth.
description.nl: Een zeskantige afstandsbus (male-female) voor M4: een zeskant van 8 mm sleutelwijdte en 20 mm lang, staand op het XY-vlak, met de Z-as als as en twee hoekpunten op de X-as. Bovenop een M4-tapeind van 8 mm lang (een cilinder van 4 mm) met uitwendige M4-draad over 6,5 mm vanaf het vrije eind; onderin een tapgat: een boorgat van 3,3 mm, 10 mm diep, met inwendige M4-draad over 8 mm vanaf de onderkant. De draad mag cosmetisch zijn. Stuur hem met de variabelen across_flats, length, stud_len en tap_depth.

expect.value: sqrt(3) / 2 * across_flats^2 * length + pi * (2 mm)^2 * stud_len - pi * (1.65 mm)^2 * tap_depth
sqrt(3) * across_flats^2 + 2 * sqrt(3) * across_flats * length + 2 * pi * 2 mm * stud_len + 2 * pi * 1.65 mm * tap_depth

value: (sqrt(3) / 2 * across_flats^2 * length^2 / 2 + pi * (2 mm)^2 * stud_len * (length + stud_len / 2) - pi * (1.65 mm)^2 * tap_depth^2 / 2) / (sqrt(3) / 2 * across_flats^2 * length + pi * (2 mm)^2 * stud_len - pi * (1.65 mm)^2 * tap_depth)

derivation: A regular hexagon s across flats has sides s / sqrt(3) and area sqrt(3)/2 s^2; corners on the X axis put them at X = +-s/sqrt(3), the flats at Y = +-s/2.
V = sqrt(3)/2 s^2 L + pi 2^2 ls - pi 1.65^2 dt = 1108.5 + 100.5 - 85.5 = 1123.5 mm^3. A cosmetic thread changes no volume; a modeled one would, so the threads are cosmetic here (the default).

Area: the hex's two ends sqrt(3) s^2 and six sides 6 (s/sqrt(3)) L; the stud swaps a disc of the hex top for its own top and adds its wall 2 pi 2 ls; the tap drill swaps a disc of the bottom for its floor and adds its wall.
Centroid Z: hex at L/2, stud at L + ls/2, less the drill at dt/2.

threads counts the features that put a thread on and were built: 2. The reference names the faces by the primitives they came from (F3:face(0) is the stud's wall, F3:face(2) its top; F5:face(0) the drill's wall), names that are followed through the booleans; the internal thread starts at the hex's bottom face, F2:startCap().
